solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Welsh factories rebuilt in a straight line

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Welsh factories are reconstructed along a straight row.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the shortest direct distance between two places, as a bird would travel.

clue.text: Routine toil behind what could be a Walled Society?

indicators.note: behind places the next piece after the one before it

parts.words: what could be a Walled Society
parts.note: read these letters as instructions: ALL placed in a day (Wed, short for Wednesday) gives W-ALL-ED, then S for Society
toil means labour or effort

explanation.surface: Ordinary labour carried out behind the walls of some enclosed community.
explanation.walkthrough: Read ALL IN A DAY'S as an instruction: WED is a day, so ALL inside it makes WALLED, and S is Society. 'behind' puts WORK at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something treated as an ordinary part of one's job, i.e. routine.

clue.text: Attack fuss about right sort of exercise

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fuss word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss
PE is physical education, a kind of exercise

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about the right kind of workout.
explanation.walkthrough: A to-do is a fuss; PE is the school subject physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to attack and wreck it, as a warship sinks a vessel.

clue.text: Codeword, cautionary signal, sent around Switzerland, place where voices resound

indicators.note: the two outer pieces are sent round the country code, enclosing it between them

parts.note: Echo is the NATO phonetic codeword for E
an amber traffic light warns drivers to take care
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A coded warning signal is transmitted around Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent around' means the two outer pieces surround the country code, one each side.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberant room built so that sound bounces back is where voices resound.

clue.text: Yorkshire division is up and running

definitions.meaning: Yorkshire was historically split into three administrative districts, North, East and West
a jockey who is up and going along on a horse is in the saddle and moving

explanation.surface: Some part of Yorkshire is now operating.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire's old divisions were the North, East and West Ridings; a jockey 'up' is mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a historic Yorkshire district and travelling on horseback.

clue.text: Cultured spa Berkshire town will have in good shed

parts.note: a well is a spring, as in a spa town

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so these letters are taken away from the town

parts.note: Reading is a large town in Berkshire, west of London

explanation.surface: A refined visitor from a spa goes to a Berkshire town in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' removes IN and G from READING, leaving READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cultured has read widely and is well-informed.

clue.text: On line, say

definitions.meaning: in cricket the on side of the field is also called the ... side
a stage of a journey or course, such as one stretch of a route

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket 'on side' and 'leg side' are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the cricket term for the on side and a stretch of a route.

clue.text: River containing strangely toxic things with a foreign flavour

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the river word goes round the other letters

parts.note: an ea is a river or watercourse, a word familiar from crosswords

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters of toxic are reordered

explanation.surface: A river holds weirdly poisonous items with foreign tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges 'toxic' to XOTIC, which the river word, 'containing', encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural word means curious objects from far-off lands, with a foreign flavour.

clue.text: HP deposit secures dream place

parts.note: hire purchase is colloquially called the never-never in Britain
to land is to set down or deposit

explanation.surface: A hire-purchase down payment secures an ideal home.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is hire purchase, buying on credit, which Britons call the 'never-never'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's imaginary realm is the archetypal fantasy place, an unreachable idyll.

clue.text: Suddenly pitched forward, dog almost died

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog

explanation.surface: A dog lurches forward and nearly dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LURCHER to LURCHE; a lurcher is a greyhound cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurch is to make a sudden unsteady movement, as when pitched forward.

clue.text: Husband, enthralled by opener for Leeds United score, shouted in ear

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside, so the husband letter goes within
shouted signals that the word is rendered by how it is cried out loud

parts.note: a goal is a score in football

explanation.surface: A husband is thrilled by Leeds United's opening goal, bellowed in his ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shouted' takes GOAL as it sounds, GOLE, and 'enthralled by' places H inside it after L and U.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for the ear, literally the hole in one's lug.

clue.text: Female born in poverty? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: need is poverty or want

explanation.surface: A woman was born into hardship, or nearly so.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for born is used before a married woman's maiden name.

clue.text: Metro, the London original branch that's in the red?

definitions.text: Metro, the London original branch that's in the red?

parts.words: Metro, the London original branch that's in the red?
parts.note: a branch of the London Underground metro drawn in red on the tube map, with 'original' hinting at principal or middle

explanation.surface: Which founding branch of a business is running at a loss?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' suggests debt, but the line is coloured red on the London Underground map.
explanation.definitionFit: The Underground route crossing the city east to west is shown in red.

clue.text: Perhaps Mancunian artisan can offset needing to follow Left

indicators.note: the rearranged letters must follow, so the left letter comes first
offset means set askew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Manchester craftsman can make up for being behind the left-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offset' rearranges ARTISAN CAN, which 'needing to follow' puts after L. A Mancunian, from Manchester, is in historic Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Manchester, historically in Lancashire, is an example of someone from that county.

clue.text: Robin flying back clutching the old man's trinket

indicators.note: clutching means gripping inside, so the outlaw's name goes round the father
flying back means travelling in the reverse direction, so the outlaw's name is read backwards

parts.note: Robin Hood, the legendary outlaw
the old man is slang for father, DA

explanation.surface: A robin flies home holding Dad's little ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying back' gives DOOH. Robin is the outlaw Robin Hood, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means a thingummy or knick-knack, a small trinket.

clue.text: Assert animation loses nothing when revamped

indicators.note: loses means the letter for nothing is dropped from the word
revamped means remade, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone claims an animated film shed nothing in its remake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes O from ANIMATION and 'revamped' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to insist on it, to assert that it is true.

clue.text: Virus makes bird quiet during party

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the bird and quiet letters go inside the party

parts.note: a fest is a festival or party
an owl is a bird
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A virus makes a bird keep quiet during a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is not the first word of the answer as it seems: only the owl is inside the party.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a viral disease of poultry, also called avian influenza.

clue.text: Time to reserve periodical

parts.note: a year is a period of time
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: It's time to order a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual publication is a periodical issued once in each twelve months.

clue.text: Case for a diplomat?

parts.note: suggests a briefcase carried by an embassy official, and the official himself is a junior diplomat

explanation.walkthrough: The word names both a slim document case and a junior member of an embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: The document case is named after the embassy officials who carried one.

clue.text: Famous Russian father's very loving. Not half!

parts.note: pa is father, the 's being a link

indicators.note: Not half keeps only half of the word, here its first three letters

explanation.surface: A Russian dad is extremely affectionate, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' looks like the British exclamation meaning 'very much', but it halves LOVING to LOV.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov was the celebrated Russian physiologist known for conditioning dogs.

clue.text: Neil could form part of RU formation

indicators.note: could form says the letters of the name may be rearranged into a new word

parts.note: read in reverse, the answer's second word, meaning out of order, is the part that signals the rearranging of Neil

explanation.surface: A player named Neil might join a rugby set piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as wordplay says 'LINE out': OUT, meaning disordered, is the anagram signal that turns LINE into NEIL, so it supplies no clue words. RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the forwards form two rows to contest a throw from touch.

clue.text: Like a teeming crowd when excited

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
warm can mean heated or excited

explanation.surface: A packed crowd behaves this way once roused.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming with moving people or insects, like bees crowding a hive.

clue.text: Facility initially was continuing to be expanded

definitions.text: Facility initially was continuing to be expanded

parts.words: Facility initially was continuing to be expanded
parts.note: the first letters of 'was continuing' give a familiar two-letter abbreviation, written out in full gives a toilet facility

explanation.surface: A building's amenities were at first still being enlarged.
explanation.walkthrough: W and C, the initials of 'was continuing', are a common abbreviation; expanded to its full form it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavatory is a convenience, a facility found in most buildings.

clue.text: Neither's partner is new, on the other hand

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone's companion is a newcomer, by contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'neither this nor that' the two conjunctions are paired, so it is the partner word.

clue.text: Anchorite deciphered clues in borders of Rosetta Stone

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the borders
the borders of the phrase are its outermost letters
deciphered means decoded, so the letters of clues are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hermit decoded the clues on the Rosetta Stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deciphered' turns CLUES into CLUS, which goes 'in' R and E, the borders of 'Rosetta Stone'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite lives in religious seclusion, a hermit who shuns company.

clue.text: International body lifted endless burden

indicators.note: lifted means raised, and in a down entry that reads the word upwards
endless means without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an onus is a burden or responsibility

explanation.surface: An international organisation has its never-ending load taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims ONUS to ONU; 'lifted' reverses it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations Organisation is a body uniting countries worldwide.

clue.text: Song encapsulating backward Northern Australian state

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the song goes round the other letters

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

indicators.note: backward signals that the letters are written in reverse

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia, and Australian

explanation.surface: A song holds a backward-looking northern Australian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' gives ZON. 'Australian state' is a false trail: the state is American.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty United States, in the American southwest.

clue.text: Removed corruption from type of art by crazy tainted man

parts.note: Art Deco is an interwar style of design

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A deranged polluted man ruined a piece of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges TAINTED MAN after DECO.
explanation.definitionFit: To decontaminate is to cleanse something of pollution or impurity.
